questions.q: What does selecting a Policy first typically do on the compute creation form?
options: Limits and simplifies which settings are even shown, as set up by a workspace admin
Immediately starts the cluster with no further configuration
Deletes any other compute resources in the workspace
Has no actual effect on the form
questions.explain: This keeps costs and configuration sane for everyone else in the workspace.

questions.q: How does the worker node type setting connect to Foundations Lesson 31?
options: It's where the driver/worker Spark architecture becomes a real, billable Azure VM size setting
It has no connection to anything covered in Foundations
It only affects storage, never compute
It determines the pricing tier of the workspace
questions.explain: Spark runs one executor per worker node — "worker" and "executor" are used interchangeably for this reason.

options: Databricks adds workers when the workload demands it and removes them once they're idle, between a min and max
It permanently fixes the cluster at the maximum worker count
It disables the driver node entirely
It has no effect on cost or performance
questions.explain: Without it, you commit to a fixed worker count regardless of what any given job actually needs.

questions.q: Why is automatic termination described as the single most important cost control on the compute form?
options: A running cluster bills by the hour whether or not anyone's using it, and this setting shuts it down after a period of inactivity
It's the only setting that affects the Databricks Runtime version
It has no real financial impact and is mostly a convenience feature
It only matters for job clusters, never interactive ones
questions.explain: It's trivially easy to forget when you're focused on getting a notebook working.

questions.q: What is "compute" in Databricks terminology, broadly?
options: Databricks' broader term covering both interactive clusters and job clusters
A synonym exclusively for job clusters, never interactive ones
A billing category unrelated to actual Spark clusters
Only refers to the driver node, never the workers
questions.explain: Lesson 5 covers the distinction between these two types of compute in more detail.
